intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A. In the reported families, the SCN5A mutation was found together with rare polymorphisms in the gene encoding the atrial-specific gap junction protein connexin-40 (Cx40), which may modify the phenotype.

checks.claim: Atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A.
checks.evidence_quote: familial AS was associated with the concurrence of a cardiac sodium channel mutation and rare polymorphisms in the atrial-specific Cx40 gene
checks.explanation: The abstract links an SCN5A mutation to familial AS, but only together with Cx40 polymorphisms. It does not say the mutation is heterozygous or that it alone causes AS.

checks.claim: In the reported atrial standstill families, the SCN5A mutation was found together with rare polymorphisms in the gene encoding the atrial-specific gap junction protein connexin-40 (Cx40).
checks.evidence_quote: The three living AS patients exclusively coinherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the SCN5A-D1275N mutation.
checks.explanation: The paper reports one family in which the SCN5A mutation occurred together with rare polymorphisms in the atrial-specific gap junction gene Cx40.

checks.claim: Rare Cx40 polymorphisms may modify the atrial standstill phenotype in SCN5A mutation carriers.
checks.evidence_quote: We propose that, although the functional effect of each genetic change is relatively benign, the combined effect of genetic changes eventually progresses to total AS.
checks.explanation: The authors propose that the Cx40 changes contribute to the phenotype together with the SCN5A mutation, which matches 'may modify'.

paragraphs.text: Atrial standstill is a rare arrhythmia that sometimes appears to be genetically determined (Groenewegen et al., 2003). It has been associated with several conditions, including congenital heart disease, valvular heart disease, conduction disturbances, Brugada syndrome, myocardial infarction, and amyloidosis. Familial clustering has been reported only rarely (Fazelifar et al., 2005).

paragraphs.text: In a large family with atrial standstill, Groenewegen et al. (2003) used candidate gene screening to identify a novel mutation in the SCN5A gene, asp1275-to-asn (D1275N). The mutation was present in all 3 affected living relatives and in 5 unaffected relatives, and the deceased affected relative was an obligate carrier. They also found 2 closely linked polymorphisms in regulatory regions of the Cx40 gene, at nucleotides -44 (G-A) and +71 (A-G). Eight relatives were homozygous for both polymorphisms, a genotype seen in only about 7% of control subjects, and 3 of these 8 were affected. Only the 3 living patients had inherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the D1275N mutation. Mutant D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation compared with wildtype channels, and in reporter gene analysis the rare Cx40 genotype gave less reporter expression than the more common genotype. Groenewegen et al. (2003) proposed that each genetic change has a relatively benign functional effect, but that their combined effect eventually progresses to total atrial standstill.

paragraphs.text: In an 11-year-old boy with an apparently sporadic case of atrial standstill, Makita et al. (2005) identified a novel SCN5A mutation, leu212-to-pro (L212P), which was also present in his father, who was in normal sinus rhythm. Recombinant L212P sodium channels studied by whole-cell patch clamp showed a large hyperpolarizing shift in the voltage dependence of activation (wildtype, -48.1 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P, -63.5 +/- 1.5 mV) and of inactivation (wildtype, -86.6 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P, -95.6 +/- 0.8 mV), as well as delayed recovery from inactivation. The proband, but not his father, also carried Cx40 polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother. Makita et al. (2005) concluded that SCN5A defects most likely underlie atrial standstill, and that coinheritance of Cx40 polymorphisms may modify its clinical expression.

agent.process_note: I opened all 8 files. Five older papers (Allensworth 1969, Harrison and Derrick 1969, Williams 1972, Amat-y-Leon 1974, Shah 1992) had titles only, so they are cited only for what their titles say. Three had abstracts only (Groenewegen 2003, Fazelifar 2005, Makita 2005). None of the abstracts gave nucleotide-level changes for the SCN5A mutations, so only the protein changes are given. No ancestry, consanguinity, pedigree details or ages were available except the proband's age of 11 years. No MIM numbers or chromosomal locations were supplied for SCN5A or the Cx40 gene, so none are given. I treated Cx40 as a reported modifier, not as a causal gene in relationships.
